meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 撮影中は電源オフだって！
examples.trans: We told you to switch the power off during filming!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.trans: We told you to switch the power off during filming!

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Colloquial particle adding emphasis, similar to でも or も.

examples.text: 俺だって言いたいことがある。
examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

examples.text: 誰だって間違いはある。

meanings.note: Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Cue word used before starting a race or filming.
Film/theater cue or general noun from English 'action'.

examples.text: 次のアクションを起こす。

meanings.note: Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: バッチリです！商談するアポが取れましたよ。
examples.trans: Spot on! I secured an appointment for a business talk with the president.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: バッチリです！商談するアポが取れましたよ。
examples.trans: Spot on! I secured an appointment for a business talk with the president.

examples.text: アポは取れてるんですよね？
examples.trans: You did confirm our appointment, right?

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).

examples.text: 一度食べてみてください。
やってみなければ分かりません。
examples.trans: You won't know unless you try.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Special reading きょう.

examples.text: ちなみに今日の夕方なんですけど、いかがですか？
examples.trans: By the way, it is for this evening—does that work for you?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Confident everyday word that works either before a predicate or as a standalone answer.

examples.text: もちろん手伝いますよ。

meanings.note: Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.text: 会議は何時に終わりますか。
examples.trans: What time does the meeting end?

meanings.note: Conjunctive particle giving a reason, softer than から.

examples.text: 雨が降っているので、家にいます。
examples.trans: Since it's raining, I'm staying home.

examples.text: 時間がないので急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: We don't have time, so let's hurry.

meanings.note: Formal/polite transition; contracts to それじゃ or じゃあ in casual speech.

examples.text: それでは始めましょう。

meanings.note: Satisfied exclamation when gearing up or finishing a task cleanly.

examples.text: よし、いくぞ！甘やかすな！
examples.trans: All right, let's roll! Stop coddling the actor!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
